name: 얼음 동굴 바위벽 방(빙판 바닥) — 바닥·벽면을 조립기와 같은 천장 띠(벽 윗면) 사이에 조립(위에서 본 3/4 방 한 칸)
label: atlas_biome_interior/plus/room-rock-ice
reasons: 화풍: 윤곽이 근흑(재질 어두운 톤 아님) (4/4)

answer.evidence: This is a one-room diorama: a dark brown rock back wall face (rows 31-63, 33 rows) with a thin gray top edge band (rows 28-30, edge line at row 30, darker shadow below), and a large icy floor (rows 64-175) seen from above. The side walls are only 1-2 px outline strips, not receding side faces. The wall face and floor give a 3/4 reading, but the wall top band is thin, only about 3 rows, and the room has no roof or ceiling. I counted the floor as the main top surface.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a room interior (ice floor plus a rock ceiling band) rather than a roof/wall/door building, but it is judged on craft against the building references. Measured facts: 6 colours per tile against 18 and 11 for the references, and 57 distinct colours against 185 and 66. Flat-fill coverage is 26% while both references are at 0%. 100% of dark edge pixels are near-neutral, against 7% and 9% for the references, so the outline is a neutral dark frame and not a tinted material tone. By eye, the ice floor uses only about 3 pale blue steps, with dithered patches and a few crack lines, so it has some texture but little shading depth. The dark frame and the border around the rock band read as a flat, sticker-like edge. The rock band at the top is better, with several brown tones and speckle. Overall the piece is shallower than the Beodeul references on every measure.

surfaces.part: back rock wall (north interior face, vertical)

answer.evidence: The main body is a large flat ice floor (rows ~64-176) seen from above. The only vertical face is the rock wall on the north (back) side, rows 31-63, which is an interior back wall, not a south face. Along the south edge there is only a 1-row edge line near row 176 with no front face below it. The left and right walls are 1-px lines. The dark rows 0-27 and the rows below the floor are background. The object has no south front face of 3+ rows, so it reads as a top-down slab with a back wall.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a room interior (ice floor plus a rock wall band), set against house exteriors with a roof, walls and a door. The kind is still treated as matching, so judging it on structure and shading craft. The measured facts count against it. It has 6 colours per tile against 18 and 11 in the references, and 57 distinct colours against 185 and 66. Flat-fill coverage is 26% against 0% in both references. All of its dark edge pixels are near-neutral (100%), where the references sit at 7% and 9%. The picture agrees. The frame and the dark border are neutral near-black and read as a sticker-style outline. The ice floor is mostly pale blue with sparse speckle, crack marks and a few blob patches, which gives roughly 3-4 lightness steps. The large pale areas are close to flat. The rock band at the top has some mottled brown texture but only a few steps. Overall it is shallower than both references in shading steps, outline tint and tile density.

answer.evidence: Rows 0-27 are a dark void above the room. Rows 28-30 are a thin grey ledge cap whose lightness falls from 134 to 78. Rows 31-63 are the back rock wall, a vertical face 33 rows tall. Rows 64-175 are the large ice floor, a horizontal surface seen from above, closed by a light edge line near row 176. The side walls are only 1px outlines, not receding side faces. The structure is a one-room cutaway with a back wall face and a visible floor, not a flat slab or a pure front elevation. The wall-top cap is only about 3 rows and works as a rim, so the top surface here is mostly the floor.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is an ice-floor room, not a building with roof, walls and door, so it does not match the reference kind. Measured facts: 6 colours per tile against 18 and 11 for the references, 57 distinct colours against 185 and 66, and 26% flat-fill coverage against 0% for both references. 100% of its dark edge pixels are neutral, against 7% and 9% for the references, so the frame and edges are a neutral black/grey line with no material tint. The ice floor has pale blue speckle, dither patches and cracks, which is some texture, but only about 4 lightness steps. The dark rock band at the top has some grain. The large near-black bands above and below the room are flat fills. Overall it is shallower and flatter than the references and reads as a sticker-like frame.

surfaces.part: ice floor (open room interior seen from above)

answer.evidence: This is a one-room interior seen from the south. The back wall has a light grey cap at rows 28-30 that darkens toward row 30, with dark shadow at rows 31-35. Below it is a brown rock wall face of about 33 rows (rows 31-63), a vertical front face. The large ice floor at rows 64 to about 175 is a horizontal surface seen from above, and it reads as the open interior of the room. The left and right edge strips are only 1-2 px lines, not receding side faces. The south edge is a thin grey line with no front wall. The wall-top band is thin, so the top surface depends on whether the floor counts as the main top.

styleAnswer.evidence: Measured facts put the candidate well below both references. It has 6 colours per tile against 18 and 11, and 57 distinct colours against 185 and 66. Flat-fill coverage is 26% where both references are at 0%. Its dark edge pixels are 100% near-neutral, against 7% and 9% for the references, so the outline is a neutral near-black frame and not a dark tone of the adjacent material. By eye, the room is a framed rectangle with a dark rock band on top and a pale icy floor. The floor has mottled blotches and a few crack lines, but it stays within about 3 light-blue steps. The rock band is only a few brown-grey tones with little per-stone shading. Large dark border areas are flat fills. There is no roof, door or window structure and no per-material ramp like the references' roof tiles, plaster or stones. Next to the references it looks flatter and thinner, and the outline reads as a sticker frame.
